findings.title: Project reference is substituted for immutable deployment identity
findings.exact_defect: validatePrivateRuntimeLiveEnvironmentAuthorityV1 passes liveEnvironmentAttestation.vercel_project_reference as deploymentId. Protected-edge configuration, internal assertions, and replay fingerprints therefore bind to a project reference rather than the exact immutable deployment or artifact.
findings.security_effect: Cross-deployment authority ambiguity remains for deployments sharing the same Vercel project, configuration, and signing material.
required_behavior: Use a reviewed immutable deployment identity from the exact live environment attestation, separate from the Vercel project reference.
Require configuration deployment_id to equal the immutable attested deployment identity.
Keep the immutable identity in internal assertions and replay fingerprints.
Deny same-project but different-deployment, stale-deployment, and missing-deployment cases.
permitted_repair_boundary: protected-edge configuration and attestation validation files explicitly authorized by a repair campaign
src/lib/intelligenceFabric/coachConnect/productionSecurity/protectedEdgeIdentity/internalAssertion.js only if the existing field cannot be preserved
existing environment, contract, assertion, and integration tests
required_tests: same project and exact deployment allows
same project and different immutable deployment denies
stop_conditions: Vercel inspection or deployment is required
a second identity authority is introduced
attestation schema expansion lacks separate architecture authority

findings.title: SESSION_BOUND mode has no trusted session binding
findings.exact_defect: The replay fingerprint contains token_identifier_ref, canonical_subject_ref, environment_id, and deployment_id only. In SESSION_BOUND mode, an idempotent CLAIM_REPLAY result is accepted without a trusted server session, transaction, browser binding, or request-context binding.
findings.security_effect: A stolen upstream bearer token can be reused until expiry from another request context, with each reuse minting a fresh one-time internal assertion.
required_behavior: Fail closed for SESSION_BOUND until a trusted binding exists, or bind reuse to a cryptographically established server-derived session or transaction identifier.
Include the trusted binding in the authoritative atomic replay fingerprint.
Reject absent, mismatched, cross-session, concurrent, and post-logout reuse.
Preserve outage fail-closed behavior and no local fallback.
permitted_repair_boundary: existing protected-edge focused, configuration, and integration tests
required_tests: same token and same trusted session follows the reviewed policy
same token and different trusted session denies
same token and attacker-controlled binding denies
concurrent reuse has one valid winner where exclusivity is required
stop_conditions: binding would be client asserted or inferred from an untrusted header or cookie
unqualified provider behavior must be trusted

findings.title: Contradictory temporal claims are accepted
findings.exact_defect: The upstream verifier does not require exp to be later than iat, and the internal assertion verifier does not explicitly require expires_at to be later than issued_at. Clock skew can therefore admit internally contradictory signed time claims.
findings.security_effect: Malformed but cryptographically valid claim sets can establish protected-edge identity, contradicting the fail-closed temporal doctrine and producing inconsistent audit semantics.
required_behavior: Require coherent ordering among nbf, iat, auth_time, and exp.
Require internal assertion expires_at to be strictly later than issued_at.
Apply clock skew to server-time comparisons only, not to contradictory intra-token ordering.
required_tests: auth_time later than iat or exp denies under the reviewed policy
